newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cambodia's Ranariddh back in Cambodia - aide.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Ranariddh back in Cambodia - aide.

text.p: Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh has left France and is back in Cambodia, an official of his FUNCINPEC party in France told Reuters on Sunday.
"He is currently back in Cambodia," Chanrith Yao, the head of the FUNCINPEC party in France, told Reuters.
Heavy fighting raged in Phnom Penh for a second day on Sunday as forces loyal to Ranariddh battled those supporting his rival, Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
A second key Cambodian political figure in France, opposition leader Sam Rainsy, told Reuters that Ranariddh had left France and was headed for Bangkok.

Rainsy, a former Cambodian finance minister and now head of the officialy unrecognised Khmer Nation Party, said the first prime minister had intended to return to Cambodia by land from Bangkok as scheduled flights into the Asian nation have all been cancelled.
Rainsy is a bitter political foe of Hun Sen and allied with Ranariddh. The two prime ministers head a fractured coalition government formed after a United Nations-run election in 1993.

Rainsy said he had information from Bangkok that forces loyal to Ranariddh had destroyed several tanks controlled by Hun Sen's troops and were headed south to the town of Pak Mao, Hun Sen's stronghold 15 km (10 miles) south of the capital.
